name: Burg Berneck
kurzbeschreibung: The High Medieval rock castle Burg Berneck perches spectacularly above the Kaunertal gorge and once served Emperor Maximilian I as a hunting lodge.
oeffnungszeiten: Juli bis September nur im Rahmen wöchentlicher Führungen (Voranmeldung)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Burg Berneck (also known as Schloss Berneck) is one of the most daringly positioned and exceptionally preserved Gothic residential castles in all of Tyrol. It perches atop a prominent rocky outcrop at 1,076 metres above sea level in the municipality of Kauns at the entrance to the Kaunertal valley in the Tyrolean Oberland. On three sides, the rock face drops almost vertically some 130 metres into the rushing Faggenbach gorge. This historic stronghold captivates visitors with its intact medieval defensive architecture and affords panoramic vistas over the Inntal valley and the glaciated peaks of the Kaunergrat.

History & Architecture

The castle was first documented in 1225, erected by the Rhaetian noblemen Herren von Berneck. During the Rottenburg Feud in 1410, the troops of the Tyrolean sovereign Herzog Friedrich IV. mit der leeren Tasche besieged the stronghold and conquered it following intense bombardment with catapults. A historic chapter began in 1501: The future Emperor Maximilian I. acquired the castle from Hans von Fliehs in an exchange for Schloss Tratzberg. Maximilian valued the complex for prolific chamois hunting in the high valleys of the Kaunertal, substantially expanding the residential quarters, defensive fortifications, and castle chapel. After centuries of changing ownership, the monument fell into ruins until it was purchased in 1976 by Innsbruck architect DI Ekkehard H?rmann and his wife Dr. Magdalena H?rmann. In a multi-decade private restoration effort, they rescued the architectural masterpiece and were honoured in 1986 with the prestigious Europa-Nostra-Diplom. The art-historical centerpiece is the late Gothic St.-Bartholom?us-Kapelle (c. 1437) featuring ribbed vaulting and rare wall frescoes.

Visit & Getting There

Because Burg Berneck is privately owned by a family, interior viewings are possible exclusively as part of guided tours during the summer months (July to September). Guided tours take place weekly on set days (usually Thursday and Friday mornings). Advance booking through the Kaunertal Tourist Board or directly via info@burg-berneck.at is mandatory. Admission fees for the tour: Adults approx. ? 5.00 to ? 7.00, children approx. ? 3.00 to ? 4.00 (discounted with the regional Tiroler Oberland guest card). Public transport: By train to Landeck-Zams station, from there take Postbus route 210/230 to the Kauns Dorfplatz stop (approx. a 15-minute downhill walk to the castle). By car: Via the Inntalautobahn A12 or Arlbergschnellstra?e S16 to Prutz, then up the Kaunerberg provincial road L243 to Kauns; parking is available at the municipal office or right before the castle access bridge.

Tips

Due to historic terrain with uneven cobblestones, narrow portals, and stairs, the castle complex is not barrier-free; sturdy footwear and surefootedness are essential. The vertigo-inducing view from the wooden approach bridge straight down into the gorge is breathtaking. Combine your visit with a hike along the Kauner Kulturwanderweg cultural trail or an excursion to the Naturparkhaus Kaunergrat at Gachenblick.
